quote: let the reader hold this image
note: An exercise for the imagination. Take the twenty-four brightest stars in the sky and rearrange them as two rings, one inside the other. That gives a faint idea of the two circles of twelve souls turning around Dante.
The astronomer Ptolemy counted fifteen stars of the first magnitude, the brightest class. To these Dante adds the seven of the Great Bear and two of the Little Bear, making twenty-four.
The seven stars of the Plough, or Big Dipper. Seen from Europe they circle the pole without ever setting.
The Little Bear, pictured as a horn. Its narrow tip is the Pole Star, at the end of the axis on which the heavens turn. The two bright stars at its wide end are its "mouth".

context: It turns around the axis that runs through the Pole Star.

note: Dante calls her only "the daughter of Minos". In Ovid, the god Bacchus took the garland from her head and set it in the sky as the constellation of the Northern Crown, a ring of stars. Dante has it happen at her death.

quote: one spins forward, one spins back
note: Dante's Italian is obscure here. It is usually read as the two rings turning in opposite directions, though some take it to mean that one leads and the other follows.
A river of Tuscany that in Dante's day crept through marshes, hardly moving. The "swiftest heaven" is the Primum Mobile, the fastest thing in the universe.
The ancient pagans sang hymns to Bacchus, god of wine, and Apollo, god of the sun and of poetry. These souls sing of the two central mysteries of Christian faith.

quote: divine and human joined in one Person
note: The Incarnation: Christ is one Person with two natures, fully God and fully man.
From the task of dancing and singing to the task of teaching Dante. Each gives them joy.

context: He takes up the second of the two puzzles he set aside in Canto 11.

note: The first puzzle, about the Dominicans growing fat, was settled in Canto 11. The second is how Thomas could say in Canto 10 that no one ever rose to equal Solomon in wisdom.
Adam's. God took a rib from his side to make Eve (Genesis 2).

context: Her "taste" is her eating of the forbidden fruit, for which the whole human race has paid.

note: Christ's. As he hung dead on the cross a soldier pierced his side with a spear (John 19).
Christ's death paid for every human sin, those committed before it and those to come.
Dante's objection. Adam and Christ the man were made directly by God, so they must have had all the knowledge a human being can hold. How, then, could Solomon be the wisest?

context: He was the fifth soul Thomas pointed out in the first ring, in Canto 10.

note: The Word, the Son of God, in whom the Father thinks the pattern of everything that can exist. All created things, angels and stones alike, are reflections of that one thought.
The Trinity again. The Light is the Son, its Source is the Father, and the Love that joins them is the Holy Spirit.
The nine orders of angels, which turn the nine heavens. God's light is first reflected in them, as in mirrors, and passed down through the spheres to the earth.
From heaven to heaven. Each sphere receives the power from above and works on what lies below, and the power weakens as it descends.
In the language of the schools, a contingent thing is one that need not exist and does not last. These are the short-lived things of earth: plants, animals, minerals.
Animals and plants come from seed. Medieval science held that some lower creatures, and minerals, were produced without seed by the influence of the stars alone.

A seal pressed into wax. The seal is the divine Idea, the wax is matter, and the heavens do the stamping. Since the wax varies and the heavens keep changing position, the stamp comes out more or less clearly.
A famous image. Nature knows her craft perfectly, as an old master does, but her hand shakes. So nothing she makes is quite as perfect as the idea of it.

quote: fervent Love and the clear Vision
note: The three Persons once more: Love is the Holy Spirit, Vision the Son, the first Power the Father. When God makes something directly, without nature as a go-between, the result is perfect.
The dust of the ground from which God formed Adam with his own hands (Genesis 2). Adam was therefore the perfect living creature.

context: The second time God worked directly: the conception of Christ in her womb by the Holy Spirit.

note: God appeared to the young Solomon in a dream and said, "Ask what I shall give you." He asked not for riches or long life but for an understanding heart to judge his people (1 Kings 3).

The angels who turn the heavens. How many there are was a question of theology. The questions that follow come from logic, natural philosophy and geometry: the learning of the schools, which Solomon did not ask for.
A problem in Aristotle's logic: if one premise of an argument must be true and the other only happens to be true, can the conclusion be one that must be true?
A problem in physics: whether there must be a first motion that no earlier motion caused.
A problem in geometry, and an impossible one. Any triangle drawn in a semicircle, with the diameter as its base, has a right angle, as Euclid proves.
The answer. Solomon was not the wisest of all men in every kind of knowledge. He was the wisest of kings in the wisdom a king needs: practical judgment in ruling.

Thomas's exact word in Canto 10 was that no second ever "rose" to such vision. He now explains it as the word for one who rises above his people, a king. It is a fine distinction, and Thomas knows it.

context: With Christ, "our Beloved", one of the two men who had all the knowledge human nature can hold. Solomon's wisdom was of another kind, so there is no contradiction.

note: The moral of the whole lesson, aimed at Dante and at every reader: be slow to judge. Thomas's own puzzle was a trap for anyone who jumps to conclusions.
Once we have declared an opinion, pride and attachment to it keep us from seeing that it is wrong.

context: From philosophers Thomas passes to heretics, whose hasty reasoning about Scripture was more dangerous.

note: Usually explained as the polished blade of a sword, which gives back a warped image of any face that looks into it. Others take it that the heretics hacked at Scripture and maimed it.
Common names, standing for anybody at all, like Tom, Dick and Harry. Dante's Italian has donna Berta and ser Martino.

quote: one may rise while the other falls
note: The thief may repent and be saved, the churchgoer may end in Hell. The poem has shown both: Buonconte, saved by one tear at the moment of death (Purgatorio 5), and his father Guido, damned in a friar's habit (Inferno 27). The warning also answers the old doubt about whether Solomon himself was saved.
